formation.title: The Kingdom of Ryukyu
formation.text:
The islands are united under one crown. From the coral harbors of Naha to the stone ramparts of Nakijin, the Ryukyu archipelago speaks with a single voice for the first time. Ships bearing the royal standard already call at ports from Siam to Korea, from Malacca to Ningbo. The question before us now is what kind of kingdom we shall build.

Shall Ryukyu embrace its destiny as the Bankoku Shinryo, the Bridge Between All Nations, opening its harbors to every wind and every people, growing wealthy as the indispensable intermediary of the Eastern seas? Or shall we forge the islands into a sovereign fortress-kingdom, cultivating our own martial traditions and cultural identity, beholden to no foreign power?

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: We are the Bridge Between All Nations.

modifiers.name: Bankoku Shinryo
modifiers.text: The Ryukyu Kingdom declares itself the Bridge Between All Nations, a maritime crossroads connecting the great civilizations of East and Southeast Asia through trade, diplomacy, and cultural exchange.

options.text: These islands bow to no foreign throne.

modifiers.name: Sovereignty of the Isles
modifiers.text: Under the iron hand of the Sho dynasty, the islands are welded into a unified kingdom with a distinct cultural identity, its warriors trained in the art of Te and its fortresses commanding every approach.

advances.name: Gusuku Architecture
advances.text: The distinctive curved-wall stone fortresses of the Ryukyu Islands, blending Chinese, Japanese, and indigenous construction techniques into uniquely resilient defensive works.

advances.name: Noro Priestesses
advances.text: The female spiritual leaders who preside over the sacred utaki groves and maintain the spiritual health of Ryukyuan communities through prayer and ritual.

advances.name: The Art of Te
advances.text: The indigenous fighting system of the Ryukyuan aristocracy, emphasizing unarmed combat techniques that will eventually evolve into karate.

advances.name: Island Fisheries
advances.text: Organized coastal fishing communities that sustain the island population and train the seafarers who will crew the kingdom's merchant fleet.

advances.name: Ryukyuan Seafaring
advances.text: Centuries of ocean navigation between the scattered islands of the Ryukyu chain, building the seamanship that underpins the kingdom's maritime trade.

advances.name: Sho Hashi's Unification
advances.text: The merger of the three rival Okinawan kingdoms (Hokuzan, Chuzan, and Nanzan) under a single crown at Shuri Castle in 1429.

event.title: The Three Kingdoms United
event.text:
In 1429, Sho Hashi completed what his father Sho Shisho had begun: the unification of the three rival kingdoms of Okinawa. Hokuzan, the northern mountain kingdom centered on Nakijin Castle, fell first in 1416. Nanzan, the southern domain based at Shimajiri-Oozato, submitted thirteen years later. The central kingdom of Chuzan, with its magnificent Shuri Castle remodeled after the Forbidden City itself, now commands the entire island.

Sho Hashi has adopted the Chinese hierarchical court system and established Naha as the kingdom's great harbor. The Ming Emperor has recognized his authority with an investiture seal. But how shall this new kingdom be governed?

options.text: One throne, one law, one kingdom.

modifiers.name: Unified Kingdom of Chuzan
modifiers.text: The three warring kingdoms have been united under a single throne at Shuri, bringing centralized governance and legitimacy to the Ryukyu Islands.

options.text: Let each domain keep its customs within the whole.

modifiers.name: Island Confederation
modifiers.text: Though united in name, the kingdom preserves the autonomy of its constituent domains, fostering cooperation and prosperity through consensus rather than coercion.

advances.name: Entrepot Trade Network
advances.text: The kingdom's role as maritime intermediary, re-exporting goods between China, Japan, Korea, and Southeast Asia from its central position in the East China Sea.

advances.name: Ryukyuan Lacquerware
advances.text: Luxury lacquerwork so refined that Ming envoys traveled to Ryukyu specifically to purchase it, combining Chinese techniques with distinctive Okinawan aesthetics.

advances.name: Naha Harbor
advances.text: The development of Naha as the kingdom's primary port, equipped to service the trading junks that connect Ryukyu to every major port in East Asia.

advances.name: Tribute Diplomacy
advances.text: Mastery of the Ming tributary system, securing preferential trade access and imperial recognition through careful diplomatic cultivation.

advances.name: Great Days of Chuzan
advances.text: The golden age under King Sho Shin, when the aji lords were brought to Shuri, weapons were centralized, and the arts flourished under royal patronage.

event.title: The Great Days of Chuzan
event.text:
King Sho Shin ascended the throne in 1477 and inaugurated what chroniclers would call the Great Days of Chuzan: the golden age of the Ryukyu Kingdom. His reign transformed the islands from a loose collection of feudal domains into a true centralized state.

The aji, the feudal lords, were compelled to leave their castles and reside in the capital at Shuri, where the king could watch them. Their weapons were collected and stored in the royal armory, not destroyed, but concentrated under the crown's control. The hiki system was reorganized into a disciplined force with military, police, and administrative duties.

Beyond these political reforms, Sho Shin patronized the arts with extraordinary generosity. The Sonohyan Utaki stone gate was erected as a sacred site of prayer before the king's journeys. Bingata dyeing and Ryukyuan lacquerware reached heights of sophistication that impressed even the refined courts of Beijing and Kyoto.

options.text: A golden age for the ages.

advances.name: Bingata Tradition
advances.text: The royal textile dyeing art unique to Okinawa, synthesizing Indian, Chinese, and Javanese techniques into vivid floral patterns reserved for the aristocracy.

advances.name: Tsuboya Pottery
advances.text: Consolidated ceramic production at the Tsuboya district, unifying scattered kilns into an efficient center for both domestic wares and export pottery.

advances.name: Awamori Distillation
advances.text: The traditional Ryukyuan spirit distilled from Thai rice using black koji mold, a technique brought from Siam through the kingdom's trade networks.

advances.name: Maransen Fleet
advances.text: Fast, maneuverable trading junks purpose-built for the East Asian maritime routes, carrying goods between Naha and every major port from Malacca to Ningbo.

advances.name: Bankoku Shinryo
advances.text: The Bridge Between All Nations: the declaration inscribed on the great bell of Shuri Castle, proclaiming Ryukyu's role as the maritime crossroads of East Asia.

event.title: The Bankoku Shinryo Bell
event.text:
A great bronze bell has been cast and hung at Shuri Castle, bearing an inscription that will define the kingdom for centuries to come. It reads: 'Ryukyu is a magnificent country in the South Seas, gathering the finest essence of the three kingdoms of Korea, China, and Japan. Ryukyu is the Bridge Between All Nations, and its ships are filled with the precious products of all lands.'

The Bankoku Shinryo, the Bridge Between All Nations, is more than a boast. It is a declaration of purpose. While great empires build walls and raise armies, this small island kingdom has found its power in the space between civilizations, carrying silk from China, swords from Japan, spices from Siam, and horses from Korea across the great ocean highways.

options.text: Let the bell ring across the seas.

advances.name: Dual Sovereignty
advances.text: The delicate art of maintaining tributary relations with both China and Satsuma Japan simultaneously, preserving a measure of autonomy through diplomatic ambiguity.

advances.name: Kobudo
advances.text: The ancient martial way born from weapons bans, transforming farming tools and household implements into instruments of war (bo, sai, tonfa, nunchaku) kama.

event.title: The Birth of Kobudo
event.text:
In the wake of the Satsuma invasion of 1609, the warriors of Ryukyu found themselves disarmed and subjugated. The Satsuma domain imposed strict bans on the possession of weapons, seeking to prevent any possibility of rebellion. But the spirit of the Ryukyuan warrior could not be so easily suppressed.

Farmers, fishermen, and commoners adapted the tools of their daily labor into instruments of war. The bo staff evolved from walking sticks and carrying poles. The sai emerged from modified animal prods. The tonfa came from millstone handles. The nunchaku from grain flails. The kama from harvesting sickles. The ekku from boat oars.

In secret, the traditions of Te, the indigenous martial art of the Ryukyuan aristocracy, merged with these improvised weapon techniques to create something entirely new: Kobudo, the ancient martial way. Trained in darkness, passed from master to student in absolute secrecy, this tradition would eventually give birth to karate itself.

options.text: We will never be truly conquered.

modifiers.name: Island Defiance
modifiers.text: The people of the Ryukyu Islands channel their suffering into fierce resistance, developing new martial traditions from the very tools of their daily labor.

options.text: Survival demands more than fighting spirit.

modifiers.name: Pragmatic Survival
modifiers.text: Unable to match foreign military power, the kingdom turns to cunning, maintaining its trade networks, intelligence apparatus, and diplomatic connections to preserve what sovereignty it can.

advances.name: Satsuma-Era Trade
advances.text: Under Satsuma oversight, the kingdom paradoxically expanded its trade networks, as the domain encouraged Ryukyu-China commerce to conduct indirect Japan-China trade.

advances.name: Trade Convoy Protection
advances.text: Patrol vessels defending the kingdom's merchant fleets against pirates in the East China Sea, documented as late as the turn of the 19th century.

advances.name: Island Chain Defense
advances.text: Distributed fortification across the archipelago, leveraging the natural defensive advantages of island geography against any would-be invader.

advances.name: Pechin Bureaucracy
advances.text: The administrative class that governed Ryukyu during the centuries of dual sovereignty, maintaining efficient island governance despite foreign overlordship.

advances.name: Ryukyuan Performing Arts
advances.text: The refined court traditions of Kumiodori dance-drama, sanshin music, and classical poetry that define Okinawan cultural identity.

advances.name: Sugar Cultivation
advances.text: Organized sugar cane production introduced from China, becoming a major export commodity that sustained the kingdom's economy in later centuries.

event.title: Black Sugar of the South
event.text: Gima Shinjo has come back from Fujian with the craft of boiling cane juice into black sugar, and the villages of the south ask leave to plant cane where the rice paddies lie. The cane grows where rice fails in a dry year, and Satsuma pays for sugar in silver.

options.text: Plant the cane.
Keep the rice paddies.

advances.name: Maritime Heritage
advances.text: Centuries of unbroken seafaring tradition, from the earliest inter-island voyages to the great trading expeditions of the golden age, passed down through generations.

advances.name: Karate Codification
advances.text: The systematization of the Te fighting styles into formal schools (Shuri-te, Naha-te, and Tomari-te) each encoding generations of combat wisdom into codified kata.

event.title: The Schools of Te
event.text:
Over generations, the martial traditions of the Ryukyu Islands have crystallized into distinct schools, each reflecting the character of its place of origin. Shuri-te, practiced by the aristocracy in the shadow of the royal castle, emphasizes speed, agility, and decisive strikes. Naha-te, born in the commercial port city, favors close-quarters power and breathing techniques drawn from Chinese kung fu. Tomari-te, from the fishing village between them, blends elements of both.

These styles are no longer merely techniques of self-defense. They have become a philosophical discipline, a way of understanding the body, the mind, and the relationship between them. Masters codify their knowledge into kata, precise forms that encode combat wisdom in movements that can be practiced openly without revealing their martial purpose.

options.text: The hand is mightier than the sword.

advances.name: Okinawan Identity
advances.text: The assertion of a distinct Ryukyuan cultural identity, neither Chinese nor Japanese but uniquely Okinawan, rooted in centuries of independent civilization.

advances.name: Meiji Resistance
advances.text: Defiance against forced annexation and cultural assimilation, as the Ryukyuan people struggle to preserve their language, customs, and sovereignty.

advances.name: Modern Crafts Revival
advances.text: The adaptation of traditional Ryukyuan crafts (lacquerware, bingata textiles, Tsuboya pottery) for modern markets while preserving ancestral techniques.

advances.name: Maritime Legacy
advances.text: The culmination of centuries of Ryukyuan seafaring knowledge, from coral reef navigation to open ocean passage, sustaining the islands' connection to the wider world.

destiny.name: Destiny of the Ryukyu Kingdom
destiny.text: The islands are united, the harbors teem with ships, and the world beckons. Whether as the Bridge Between Nations or as a sovereign fortress-kingdom, Ryukyu's destiny is ours to forge.

event.title: A Kingdom's Destiny
event.text: The Kingdom of Ryukyu stands at a crossroads. The islands are united, the harbors are full, and the world watches to see what this small but proud kingdom will become. The path we have chosen will define us for generations: whether we reach outward to embrace the world's trade or turn inward to forge an unbreakable island nation, the destiny of Ryukyu begins now.

options.text: Our destiny awaits.

destiny.name: Eastern Trade Hub
destiny.text: Secure control of the Japanese trade gateway at Hakata and ensure silk flows through the Ryukyuan capital market. Reach 1,000 gold to fund the expansion of the entrepot network.

conditions.text: Own Hakata, or a subject owns it

children.text: Silk is produced in the market
Silk is traded in the market

event.title: Gateway to Japan
event.text: Ryukyuan merchants now control the port of Hakata, the great gateway to Japanese trade. Ships bearing the royal standard dock alongside Chinese junks and Korean vessels, and silk from the continent flows freely through our warehouses. The entrepot network that has sustained Ryukyu for centuries now reaches into the heart of its largest market. The merchants of Naha celebrate. But the seas beyond beckon with even greater prizes.

options.text: The eastern trade is ours.

destiny.name: Dominion of the Eastern Seas
destiny.text: The great ports of Malacca and Guangzhou must fall under Ryukyuan influence. With 2,000 gold in the treasury and the prestige of a maritime power, the kingdom commands the sea lanes of East Asia.

conditions.text: Own Malacca, or a subject owns it
Own Guǎngzhōu, or a subject owns it

event.title: Masters of the Eastern Seas
event.text:
From the Strait of Malacca to the Pearl River Delta, the Ryukyuan trade network spans the breadth of maritime Asia. Guangzhou's silk and porcelain, Malacca's spices and tin, all pass through Ryukyuan hands. No merchant fleet sails these waters without reckoning with the kingdom that sits at their crossroads.

Shall we assert our dominance through naval supremacy, protecting our routes with warships that command respect? Or shall we build a network of tributary partners, binding lesser states to our commercial empire through diplomacy and mutual dependence?

options.text: Our warships shall rule these waters.

modifiers.name: Naval Supremacy
modifiers.text: Ryukyuan warships patrol the trade routes of East Asia, ensuring safe passage for the kingdom's merchant fleet and deterring any who would challenge its maritime dominance.

options.text: Bind them to us through trade and tribute.

modifiers.name: Tributary Network
modifiers.text: A web of trade dependencies and diplomatic relationships binds lesser states to Ryukyu's commercial empire, though maintaining this network strains the kingdom's military budget.

destiny.name: The True Bankoku Shinryo
destiny.text: The ultimate realization of the Bridge Between All Nations. Control Temasek, Tondo, and Quanzhou's great port at Jinjiang. Amass 3,000 gold and earn the highest prestige to become the indispensable crossroads of global trade.

conditions.text: Own Temasek, or a subject owns it
Own Tondo, or a subject owns it
Own Jìnjiāng, or a subject owns it

event.title: The Bridge Between All Nations
event.text:
What the bell of Shuri Castle proclaimed centuries ago has at last become reality. From Temasek at the tip of the Malay Peninsula to Tondo in the Philippine archipelago, from Quanzhou's ancient harbor to the spice islands beyond, Ryukyuan ships connect every corner of the maritime world. The kingdom that once counted its wealth in coral and shellfish now holds the keys to global commerce.

Shall we consolidate this position as the world's indispensable crossroads, drawing all trade through our harbors? Or shall we leverage our connections to become the supreme diplomatic power of the eastern seas, mediating between empires?

options.text: All roads of the sea lead through Ryukyu.

modifiers.name: Crossroads of the World
modifiers.text: Ryukyu has become the indispensable nexus of global maritime trade, a position that attracts settlers, merchants, and scholars from every corner of the known world.

options.text: We shall be the arbiter of the oceans.

modifiers.name: Ocean Diplomacy
modifiers.text: The maritime kingdom's unmatched network of diplomatic connections allows it to mediate between empires, secure favorable terms, and project influence far beyond its island shores.

destiny.name: Revenge upon Satsuma
destiny.text: The humiliation of Satsuma's invasion will be repaid in kind. Seize Kagoshima, the seat of the Shimazu, with an army of at least 30,000 men and the stability to sustain a war of liberation.

conditions.text: Own Kagoshima, or a subject owns it

event.title: The Fall of Satsuma
event.text: Kagoshima burns. The great castle of the Shimazu, from which the invasion of 1609 was launched, now flies the banner of the Sho dynasty. For two centuries, the people of the Ryukyu Islands endured subjugation, their weapons confiscated, their sovereignty a polite fiction maintained for Chinese trade. No more. The martial traditions born in secret (the kobudo, the karate, the fierce island spirit that no occupier could crush) have been vindicated on the battlefield. Satsuma has reaped what it sowed.

options.text: The shame of 1609 is avenged.

destiny.name: Island Chain Dominion
destiny.text: Extend Ryukyuan sovereignty over the entire island chain from Amami Oshima to Tsushima. Field an army of 50,000 and maintain a treasury of 2,000 gold to project power across the straits.

conditions.text: Own Amami Ōshima, or a subject owns it
Own Shimoagata, or a subject owns it

event.title: Lords of the Island Chain
event.text:
The Ryukyuan kingdom now stretches from the subtropical waters around Sakishima to the cold straits of Tsushima. Every island between Okinawa and the Japanese mainland acknowledges the authority of Shuri. The question now is how to consolidate this far-flung island domain.

Shall we fortify every harbor and headland, making the archipelago an impregnable chain of island fortresses? Or shall we mobilize the warrior spirit of the island population, transforming every fisherman and farmer into a soldier ready to defend the realm?

options.text: Every island shall be a fortress.

modifiers.name: Fortress Islands
modifiers.text: Every harbor and headland in the island chain has been fortified in the gusuku tradition, creating an impregnable defensive network that deters invasion and crushes rebellion.

options.text: Every islander shall be a warrior.

modifiers.name: Warrior Mobilization
modifiers.text: The martial traditions of kobudo and karate have been systematized into a national mobilization doctrine, training every able-bodied islander to reinforce the kingdom's armies at need.

destiny.name: Shuri Ascendant
destiny.text: The ultimate assertion of Ryukyuan sovereignty. Conquer Osaka and Kyoto, the commercial and imperial hearts of Japan itself. Field 75,000 men, hold 3,000 gold, and earn the prestige befitting a continental power.

conditions.text: Own Ōsaka, or a subject owns it
Own Kyōto, or a subject owns it

event.title: The Throne of Shuri Commands the Mainland
event.text:
The impossible has been achieved. Osaka, the great commercial metropolis of Japan, and Kyoto, the seat of the imperial court itself, now answer to the Kingdom of Ryukyu. A tiny island nation, once dismissed as a vassal state fit only for tribute trade, has conquered the heartland of one of the world's great civilizations. The martial arts born from oppression (the empty-handed fighting styles, the weaponized farming tools, the fierce spirit of an unconquerable people) have carried the banner of Shuri to heights no one dared imagine.

Shall we press onward in conquest, or consolidate our island empire into an unassailable fortress?

options.text: Let no land be beyond our reach.

modifiers.name: Island Conquest
modifiers.text: The kingdom's armies march with the fierce determination of an island people who refused to be conquered, carrying the martial traditions of Ryukyu to the mainland, though naval readiness suffers as resources flow to land campaigns.

options.text: Fortify what we have won.

modifiers.name: Island Fortification
modifiers.text: The hard-won conquests are secured through rapid fortification and mobilization, transforming every new territory into another link in the island kingdom's impregnable chain.

units.name: Maransen
units.text: Fast Ryukyuan trading junks optimized for the East Asian maritime routes, combining Chinese shipbuilding techniques with local seamanship.

units.name: Kobudo Militia
units.text: Fighters armed with improvised weapons (bo, sai, tonfa, nunchaku) born from the weapons bans that forced the Ryukyuan people to transform everyday tools into instruments of war.

units.name: Umibune
units.text: Ryukyuan patrol vessels designed to protect the kingdom's trade convoys against pirates in the East China Sea.

units.name: Patrol Junk
units.text: Lighter Ryukyuan vessels mobilized through the levy system for coastal defense and anti-piracy operations.

buildings.name: Ryukyuan Trading House
buildings.text: A commercial warehouse and brokerage serving the kingdom's entrepot trade, facilitating the exchange of goods between Chinese, Japanese, Korean, and Southeast Asian merchants.

buildings.name: Utaki Shrine
buildings.text: Sacred groves and prayer sites presided over by Noro priestesses, the spiritual heart of Ryukyuan communities where prayers are offered for good harvests and safe voyages.

buildings.name: Bingata Workshop
buildings.text: A royal textile workshop producing the vibrant dyed fabrics unique to the Ryukyu Kingdom, with patterns reserved for different ranks of the aristocracy.

buildings.name: Lacquerware Workshop
buildings.text: A workshop producing the exquisite Ryukyuan lacquerware prized throughout East Asia, combining multiple coats of lacquer with intricate decorative techniques.

buildings.name: Tsuboya Kiln
buildings.text: A consolidated pottery production center in the Tsuboya tradition, firing both functional domestic wares and the large storage jars used for aging awamori.

buildings.name: Awamori Distillery
buildings.text: A distillery producing the traditional Ryukyuan spirit from Thai rice and black koji mold, aged in clay pots to develop its distinctive flavor.

buildings.name: Gusuku Fortress
buildings.text: A distinctive Ryukyuan stone fortress with gracefully curving walls, combining the defensive principles of Chinese and Japanese military architecture with indigenous construction techniques.

buildings.name: Ryukyuan Harbor
buildings.text: Improved port facilities designed to service the trading junks that connect the Ryukyu Kingdom to every major port in East and Southeast Asia.

buildings.name: Karate Dojo
buildings.text: A training hall where the systematized martial arts of Shuri-te, Naha-te, and Tomari-te are taught, producing disciplined fighters from the island population.

buildings.name: Ryukyuan Sugar Mill
buildings.text: A village crushing house where oxen turn the rollers and the cane juice is boiled down into black sugar, a craft brought from China that became one of the kingdom's most valuable exports. Where the land grows cane, it yields more sugar.

where.text: The location's raw material is Sugar

buildings.name: Ryukyuan Fishing Settlement
buildings.text: An organized coastal fishing community providing both sustenance and maritime training for the island population.

children.text: Fish is produced in the market

buildings.name: Grand Entrepot
buildings.text: The ultimate expression of Ryukyu's role as the Bridge Between All Nations: a vast trading complex where goods from every corner of maritime Asia are stored, graded, and re-exported across the world.

buildings.name: Shuri Citadel
buildings.text: A magnificent fortress-palace in the tradition of the great gusuku, seat of the Sho dynasty's martial sovereignty over an island empire that now commands respect from continental powers.

list.name: Sanshikan Council of Three
list.text: The three sessei-rank chief ministers (sansoshi), drawn from the Sho-kin princely line and the senior peerage, who collectively governed beneath the king after Sho Shin's reforms (r. 1477-1526). Each minister held a portfolio (interior, finance, ritual) and decisions required consensus among the three. The Sanshikan signed Ryukyuan diplomatic correspondence and formally received Chinese investiture envoys at Shuri-jo, articulating a conciliar executive that survived nearly four centuries until the Meiji abolition of 1879.

list.name: Magiri District Administration
list.text: The kingdom's territorial subdivision into magiri (rural districts), each administered by a jito-dai or magiri-shu officer reporting to the royal court. The magiri organised cultivator levies for corvee labour, rice taxation in kind, and the gozaisho corvee for tribute-junk construction at Naha. Codified in the Ryukyu-koku Yuraiki and later registry rolls, the magiri displaced the older aji-clan holdings as the operative unit of royal administration, a centralising stroke that reached every village utaki and every fisher-hamlet on the archipelago.

list.name: Hiki Naval Rotation
list.text: The Naha-jo dock organisation that crewed the kingdom's ocean-going junks (shinko-sen) on a rotating duty system. Three hiki corps (Setado, Aragusuku, and Yagachi in the Sho Shin rolls) cycled responsibility for the biennial tribute voyages to Fuzhou, sappushi reception duty when Ming envoys arrived, and patrol of the Sakishima approaches against Wako pirate squadrons. Each hiki maintained its own warehouses, rope-walks, and seasoned sailors at Naha harbour, giving the small kingdom a disciplined maritime arm out of all proportion to its population.

list.name: Kumemura Chinese-Diaspora Administration
list.text: The Min-jin Sanju-roku Sei, the Thirty-Six Families settled by the Hongwu emperor at Kume village near Naha in 1392. Their hereditary descendants supplied the kingdom with classical-Chinese scribes, navigators trained in the Hai-tao Zhen-jing, interpreters for tribute missions, and the Confucian-scholar staff of the chancery. Kumemura ran its own Confucian school, the Meirindo (founded 1718), and produced the sapposhi reception protocols that governed every Ming and Qing investiture ceremony down to the kingdom's last days.

list.name: Tribute Mission Apparatus
list.text: The dedicated Shinko-sho registry organising the kingdom's biennial tribute embassies to the Ming (and after 1644 the Qing) court at Fuzhou and Beijing, with parallel deputations to the Satsuma daimyate at Kagoshima after the 1609 Shimazu invasion. The apparatus prepared sappo gifts of sulphur, refined sugar, horses, and lacquerware; licensed the embassy junks; and trained the seii-shi mission heads in the protocols of dual sovereignty: presenting Ryukyu as a Chinese tributary in Beijing while quietly rendering tribute to Edo through Kagoshima.

list.name: Goseki Senior Peerage
list.text: The formalised peerage hierarchy of Wo-ji, Aji-ufu, Aji, Oyakata, and Pechin that under Sho Shin consolidated the older aji-clan lords into a court-resident nobility ranked by hachimaki cap colour. The Goseki council ratified rank advancement, registered new fiefs into the kingdom's rolls, and policed precedence at Shuri court. The system bound the fractious island lords (formerly autonomous masters of Hokuzan, Nanzan, and the Sakishima) into a single rank-conscious aristocracy clustered around the throne.

list.name: Omoro Saushi Liturgical Court
list.text: The priestly office of the Kikoe-Ogimi (supreme noro priestess, traditionally the sister of the reigning king) presiding over the realm's noro priestesses and the compilation of the Omoro Saushi, the kingdom's twenty-two book liturgical anthology of sacred song compiled between 1531 and 1623. The Kikoe-Ogimi performed the king's investiture rites at Sefa-Utaki, sanctified the inter-island noro hierarchy that bound the archipelago into a single ritual-political fabric, and formalised the female-priestess complement to the male court at Shuri.
